findings.issue: The bytecode makes two stores to slot 3 (cur.val, then the whole slot with cur.has); splitting the second whole-slot store into fields re-prints 'read = stor4', a field rewritten with the value it already holds. The values just stored (0) are also not forwarded.
findings.rule: When a whole-slot store is split into field stores, omit fields whose new value equals their current value; forward a field's last stored value to later reads of it in the same path (read = 0, stor3_128 = 0).

findings.source: osm.sol:166-170 for(uint i = 0; i < a.length; i++) { require(a[i] != address(0), ...); bud[a[i]] = 1; }
findings.issue: Elements of a dynamic calldata array print as raw calldata arithmetic although the text already names the array (a, a.length). Corpus-wide 11170 lines in 171 texts contain cd[32 * idx + X + 36].
findings.rule: Print cd[32 * i + p + 36], where p is a decoded dynamic-array parameter whose bounds were checked, as p[i] (P16 extended to dynamic calldata arrays).

notes: Both source loops (kiss/diss of address[]) are readable while loops. The pack maps kiss(address[])/diss(address[]) to the single-address sources and marks kiss(address)/diss(address) as not found; the real sources are osm.sol:157-175, compared as such. LibNote's anonymous log4 prints as 'log call.func_hash: 32, 224, call.data[0 len 224], indexed caller, indexed <cd[4]>, indexed cd[36]' after the body, as in the source; for the array overloads 'indexed a' is the offset word cd[4] - consistent with the text's convention. prev()'s require(hop != 0) is folded with the modulo into a helper SafeMath.mod (exact). pass() keeps add()'s unmessaged require. peek ok is a bool decoded without validation (ABI decoder v1) - 'if ext_call.return_data[32]' is exact. No storage layout in the build (solc 0.5.10); the text's slots match the source order (cur at 3, nxt at 4, bud at 5).
summary: Faithful, compact text; only cosmetic issues: a field rewritten with its own value in void(), and calldata array elements printed as raw calldata arithmetic.
